description: Implement a character name reveal system and fix the Mira naming branch to properly respect the player's choice throughout the entire game
steps: 1. In js/engine.js, add a 'revealed_names' map to the engine state (e.g., state.revealedNames = {}). Create a new step type 'reveal_name' that marks a character id as revealed: { type: 'reveal_name', char: 'mira', name: 'Mira' }. This sets state.revealedNames[charId] = displayName.

2. In js/engine.js doSay(), modify the name resolution logic. Instead of always using charDef.name, check: if state.revealedNames[step.char] exists, use that. Otherwise, use '???' (for characters that haven't been revealed yet). Certain characters should be exempt from the reveal system (erdan, guard, servant, noble, crowd, attendant, knight, herald, pope, unknown, vision) - these always show their defined name. Add a 'revealExempt' list or mark them in characters.js.

3. In data/characters.js, add a property 'revealExempt: true' to characters that should always show their name from the start: erdan, guard, servant, noble, crowd, attendant, knight, herald, pope, unknown, vision. Main story characters (mira, seraya, elisabeth, mernel, kina, gux, ren, marcel, kuger, tenebrim, ren_ro, torren, guthethya, fiero, night, nare) should NOT be exempt - they start as '???'.

4. Add 'reveal_name' steps at the appropriate narrative moments in scene files. Key reveals: (a) data/scenes/prologue.js - reveal 'elisabeth' as 'Queen Elisabeth' when she introduces herself, reveal 'pope' as 'Pope Almert' when he speaks (actually pope is already exempt via unknown-like usage). (b) data/scenes/ch01_summoning.js - reveal 'mernel' as 'Mernel' and 'kina' as 'Kina' when they are introduced in the testing chamber. (c) data/scenes/ch01_summoning.js ch01_room_arrival - do NOT reveal 'mira' here. She is '???' at this point since she has no name. (d) data/scenes/ch02_mira.js ch02_name_mira - reveal 'mira' as 'Mira' after Erdan names her. (e) data/scenes/ch02_mira.js ch02_no_name - do NOT reveal mira. She should display as '???'. Later, add a reveal as 'Slave' based on the context (when the servant calls her that, or when Erdan internally refers to her that way). (f) data/scenes/ch02_mira.js ch02_dining - after the servant says 'Miss Mira', reveal 'mira' as 'Mira' ONLY if mira_named flag is set (use an 'if' step). If mira_unnamed, reveal as 'Slave' or keep as '???'.

5. Continue adding reveal_name steps: (g) data/scenes/ch03_palace.js - reveal 'gux' as 'Gux' when he introduces himself, reveal 'ren' as 'Ren' when Mira identifies him, reveal 'marcel' as 'Marcel' when he introduces himself. (h) data/scenes/ch04_attack.js - reveal 'elisabeth' (if not already) when she appears for the audience. The tenebrim warrior doesn't reveal his name (stays '???' or 'Tenebrim Warrior'). (i) data/scenes/ch05_sanctum.js - reveal 'kuger' as 'Kuger' when he speaks, reveal 'torren' as 'Torren' and 'guthethya' as 'Guthethya' when they introduce themselves. (j) data/scenes/ch06_seraya.js - reveal 'seraya' as 'Seraya' when Kuger introduces her.

6. Fix the Mira naming branch (ch02_no_name path): In data/scenes/ch02_mira.js ch02_no_name, set a flag { mira_unnamed: 1 } (already done). In ch02_dining, the scene currently hard-codes dialogue with 'Mira' - there are lines where Erdan says 'Mira' and the servant says 'Miss Mira'. Add conditional branching: if mira_unnamed flag is set, Erdan should say 'Hey, you' or 'Let us go inside' without using a name. The servant line 'Miss Mira' should become 'your slave' or just refer to her generically.

7. Audit ALL scenes for hard-coded 'Mira' references in dialogue text that would be spoken when the no-name branch is active. Key scenes to fix: (a) ch02_dining - Erdan says 'I meant Mira' which is impossible if he never named her. Add an if-branch: if mira_unnamed, use different dialogue. (b) ch03_palace.js ch03_gux_ren - Mira introduces herself by speaking; if unnamed, her lines stay but Erdan's internal reference is already a thought (fine). (c) ch03_palace.js ch03_tame_night - the line 'You gave me a decent name, didn't you?' from Mira ONLY makes sense if he named her. Add conditional: if mira_unnamed, skip this line or replace with something else. (d) ch04_attack.js - 'Mira' used in say steps: these reference the character id, which is fine for the engine, but Erdan says 'Please don't call yourself that' which is fine. However, the line 'Alright Mira' - if she has no name, Erdan wouldn't say it. (e) ch07_escape.js, ch08_recovery.js, ch09_ball.js, ch10_departure.js, ch11_continuation.js - audit 'Mira' in dialogue text and add conditionals where the player character uses her name.

8. In js/engine.js, implement the 'reveal_name' step handler. Add it to handleStep switch. The handler should: set state.revealedNames[step.char] = step.name, then call setTimeout(runStep, 0) to continue. Also handle a conditional reveal: { type: 'reveal_name', char: 'mira', name: 'Mira', condition: { flag: 'mira_named', op: '>=', value: 1 } } - only reveal if condition is met.
9. In js/engine.js snapshot() and restore(), include revealedNames in the snapshot so saves preserve the reveal state.

10. For the dining scene specifically, split ch02_dining into two paths after the guard interaction: ch02_dining_named (current content with 'Mira' references) and ch02_dining_unnamed (modified content where Erdan doesn't use her name, servant doesn't call her 'Miss Mira', and the 'I meant Mira' line is removed or replaced). Use an if-branch at the start of ch02_dining to route to the correct version.
11. Ensure the backlog also uses the revealed name (not the raw character name) by passing the resolved display name to state.backlog.push() in doSay().
acceptance_criteria: Characters show as '???' in the speaker name box until their name is narratively revealed
After a character is introduced/named in dialogue, their speaker name updates to their actual name
In the no-name branch (ch02_no_name), Mira is never displayed as 'Mira' - she shows as '???' and then as 'Slave' (or stays '???')
The dining scene dialogue changes when mira_unnamed flag is set: no 'I meant Mira' line, no 'Miss Mira'
The ch03 'You gave me a decent name' line from Mira is skipped/replaced when mira_unnamed is set
Generic characters (guard, servant, etc.) always show their defined name without needing a reveal
Erdan always shows as 'Erdan' (exempt from reveal system)
python3 tests/test_walk.py still passes after all changes
verification: Run: python3 tests/test_walk.py and confirm all scenes reachable and all endings accessible
Open index.html in a browser, start new game, verify first characters show as '???' until introduced
Play through the naming choice selecting 'Don't bother', verify Mira is never called 'Mira' in any subsequent scene
findings: Implementation complete. 70 scenes parsed, all 15 endings reachable. The dining scene was split into ch02_dining (router), ch02_dining_named, and ch02_dining_unnamed. The ch03_tame_night 'decent name' line was split into ch03_night_name_named, ch03_night_name_unnamed, and ch03_night_name_continue sub-scenes. The test_walk.py regex correctly picks up the new scene references via target/then/else patterns. No pre-existing test failures.
